claims.text: The starting TiVNbTa alloy has a single-phase BCC, dendritic microstructure.
The TiVNbTa alloy has a lower-temperature yield strength of approximately 800 MPa.
At 1273 K, the baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa.
At 1273 K, the baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 30% strain.
Solution treatment at approximately 1473–1573 K followed by quenching will retain a supersaturated BCC matrix.
Ageing at approximately 973 K for tens of minutes to a few hours will induce a fine, homogeneous dispersion of coherent nanoscale precipitates in the BCC matrix.
The proposed precipitates may be Ta-rich or Ti-rich B2 or other ordered intermetallic phases.
The nanoscale precipitates will impede dislocation motion.
The precipitates will delay elevated-temperature recovery processes.
The precipitates will slow dynamic recovery and grain-boundary sliding.
Precipitation strengthening will preserve the alloy's microstructural stability at elevated temperature.
At 1273 K, the aged alloy is expected to attain a yield strength closer to approximately 800 MPa than the 330 MPa baseline.
The aged alloy is expected to have greater compressive strength at 1273 K than the approximately 423 MPa baseline.
The aged alloy is expected to retain ductility comparable to or better than 30–40% strain.
The intervention is applicable to an intermediate layer between W and CuCrZr operating under thermal loads around 1273 K.
Long exposure at 1273 K may coarsen the nanoscale precipitates and erode their strengthening effect.
